sources.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2 (2021)
sources.locator: Chapter 13, printed pp. 127–131 (PDF pp. 129–133), Theorem 13.1 and equations (145)–(148). The source has positive-definite isotropic prior/noise covariances; singular and general-covariance extensions are proved locally.
sources.disposition: used; complete proof route inspected, with local hypotheses and the orthogonality component stated explicitly

contents.name: Finite-dimensional Gaussian prior, Gaussian likelihood, and normalized posterior density
contents.reason: Chapter 13 applies Bayes to a finite-dimensional Gaussian prior and Gaussian likelihood. Its worked formula assumes positive-definite isotropic prior and noise covariance; the general positive-definite Gamma and singular C0 extension is proved locally.

contents.name: Gaussian posterior MAP and posterior mean equal the Tikhonov minimizer in the isotropic full-rank case
contents.reason: Equations (146)–(148) derive the full-rank isotropic Gaussian special case. The item locally proves covariance weighting, range restriction, singular C0, and uniqueness.

contents.name: Non-Gaussian posterior mean can differ from MAP
contents.reason: Chapter 13 explicitly warns that the conditional mean does not generally coincide with MAP outside the Gaussian model. The uniform-prior witness and its exact positive mean are proved locally.

contents.name: Rank-deficient Gaussian support and pseudoinverse coordinates
contents.reason: Chapter 13 assumes positive-definite prior covariance and does not supply the rank-deficient support statement. The eigenbasis, Penrose-equation, and support proof is local.

sources.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (full lecture notes, arXiv:1302.6989)
sources.locator: §3.1, Theorem 3.1; §3.2, Theorem 3.3 and proof for the potential-weighted posterior; §4.1, Theorems 4.2–4.3 for evidence propriety context.

contents.name: Potential-weighted posterior density and conditional-law version convention
contents.reason: The complete §3.1 Theorem 3.1 and §3.2 Theorem 3.3 proof give the normalized potential posterior as a conditional-law version almost surely. The finite-GP supplier and local density calculation supply the stronger all-datum version in this finite model.

contents.name: Evidence positivity from continuity and a lower envelope
contents.reason: The printed §4.1 positivity proof infers a uniform finite bound on a merely bounded positive-mass set, which is invalid in general. The current IP-16 supplier proves positivity with a support-neighborhood argument; the finite Gaussian case also directly satisfies the envelope M1=0.
